claims.claim: Ecosystem exploded Oct 2025 (plugin launch) to April 2026: top repos reach 22k-33k+ stars, 1000+ skill collections common.

4 characteristics of premium skills: (1) vendor ownership, (2) frontmatter discipline (trigger-rich description), (3) multi-file resources with progressive disclosure, (4) commitment-before-generation pattern.
claims.evidence: R7 premium skill case studies (Frontend Design, Remotion, Trail of Bits).

claims.claim: Top-10 community-consensus skills 2026: Frontend Design (Anthropic), Remotion, Trail of Bits Security, Agent Orchestrator/AgentSys, Book Factory, Memory Persistence, Structured Engineering Workflows, Web Extraction (Firecrawl-backed), Marketing Operations, Document Automation.
claims.evidence: Triangulation from 5+ curated lists (firecrawl, composio, medium, Snyk, blockchain-council).

claims.claim: Category distribution in curated lists: Engineering workflows 43%, Document automation 22%, Web+research 18%, Marketing/content 12%, Security 5%.
claims.evidence: R7 category analysis from top-50 lists.

claims.claim: Vendor-authored skills (highest trust tier): Anthropic (Frontend Design, commit-commands, code-review), Vercel, Stripe, Cloudflare, Netlify, Trail of Bits, Sentry, Expo, HuggingFace, Figma, Remotion.
Individual premium authors: Jeremy Longshore (CCPI), Travis Vann (awesome-claude-skills), sickn33, hesreallyhim (canonical awesome-claude-code).

Naming anti-patterns: generic names (my-skill, helper, utility, tools, assistant) prevent auto-invocation matching; specific names (programmatic-video-remotion, aesthetic-commitment-framework) trigger reliably.
claims.evidence: Community troubleshooting + R3.C3 path A dependency.

claims.claim: Frontmatter anti-patterns: empty/generic description ('Helps with coding tasks'), missing when_to_use context, missing argument-hint for interactive skills, missing allowed-tools for shell-using skills (triggers permission prompt every call).
Body bloat anti-pattern: monolithic SKILL.md >3000 tokens without resources; exceeds ~1500 token body budget; high ejection risk after compaction.
Configuration anti-pattern: boolean prop proliferation (isCompact:true + showHeader:false + isRounded:true). Better: single enum variant field.
claims.evidence: Analog from UI design systems applied to skill config.

claims.claim: LLM-default-output anti-pattern: skill that doesn't force commitment gets statistical-mean output (Inter font, purple gradient, grid cards). Fix: explicit commit-before-generate (Frontend Design pattern).
Over-chaining anti-pattern: chains >5 skills incur nonlinear token cost due to listing budget + pre-invocation reasoning per step. Optimal chain depth 2-3 skills.
Testing debt: most community skills lack unit tests (golden outputs, expected behaviors); premium vendor skills (Anthropic, Remotion, Trail of Bits) include integration tests in repo.
Context pollution anti-pattern: skill loading 5000+ tokens of resources directly into main context instead of on-demand via Read; degrades compaction survival.
Hardcoded paths anti-pattern: absolute paths (C:\Users\macie\...) instead of relative (~/.claude/); breaks cross-platform portability.
Reddit/forum signal: top 3 advice for new skill authors: (1) test auto-invocation empirically, (2) measure token footprint, (3) bundle MCP with plugin when skill requires external tools.

H1->H2 2026 trends: (1) package manager consolidation toward official Anthropic marketplace, (2) vendor skills explosion, (3) signing standard emergence, (4) cross-agent compatibility, (5) localized (non-English) skills.
claims.evidence: R7 trend watch section + industry trajectory.

claims.claim: Underrepresented opportunity zones: multi-agent orchestration architecture, non-English (localized) skills, meta-skills (skills for designing skills). Maciej's system covers all 3.
claims.evidence: R7 gap analysis + Maciej project positioning.

claims.claim: Commitment-before-generation is the single highest-impact pattern for quality: forces explicit decision BEFORE output, breaking statistical-mean LLM tendency. Examples: Frontend Design (aesthetic direction), Trail of Bits (threat model).
claims.evidence: Premium skill analysis + pattern replication across top skills.

claims.claim: Security audit gap: only premium vendor skills (Remotion via Socket+Agent Trust Hub) and community-vetted (Trail of Bits skills-curated) have audit; majority of ecosystem has zero audit infrastructure.

Maciej positioning: 35 skills + 42 commands is rare orchestrator-architecture pattern, not typical skill-library pattern; unique value props are bilingual PL/EN coverage, design-first toolkit (HTML designer + encyclopedia), routing system (PRESET_CATALOG.md auto-match).
claims.evidence: CLAUDE.md project description + R7 positioning analysis.

conflicts_flagged.description: Popularity metric ambiguity: 'installs' vs 'weekly installs' vs 'stars' used interchangeably in community lists; no standardized engagement metric exists.
Ecosystem trust gap: vendor-authored skills presumed high quality (Anthropic, Remotion) but third-party skills vary widely; users lack easy way to distinguish quality tier.

gaps_flagged.description: Exact token footprint of premium skills (Frontend Design, Remotion) unknown; community infers from behavior, no public profiling.
Empirical auto-invocation reliability data: no A/B test comparing generic vs trigger-rich descriptions; advice is heuristic.
No formalized community guidelines for 'good citizenship' (naming collisions, MCP bundling standards).
No benchmark distinguishing installed vs actively-used skills; install counts may overstate real engagement.

summary: R7 catalogs 2026 ecosystem (22k-33k star awesome lists, 1000+ skills), identifies 4 premium characteristics, top-10 consensus skills, 9 anti-patterns (naming, frontmatter, body bloat, LLM-default, over-chaining, testing debt, context pollution, hardcoded paths, boolean-prop), and positions Maciej as rare orchestrator-architecture pattern with bilingual/design-first advantages.
